header.running_head: Severing Ties with the Period of Ignorance to Strengthen Ties with Islaam

blocks.text: Ummu Habeebah (RA) (the wife of Rasulullaah ﷺ). As he was gong to sit on Rasulullaah ﷺ's bedding, Hadhrat Ummu Habeebah (RA) quickly rolled it up. "Dear daughter!" Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan (RA) exclaimed, "Am I not worthy of this bedding or is it not worthy of the likes of me?" Hadhrat Ummu Habeebah (RA) replied, "This is Rasulullaah ﷺ's bedding and (you are unfit to sit on it because) you are an impure Mushrik." Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan (RA) responded by saying, "Dear daughter! You have really changed for the worse since leaving us."[^1] Another narration states that Hadhrat Ummu Habeebah (RA) added, "I would not like you to sit on his bedding."[^2]
The Statement of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) Concerning a Sparrow and its Fledglings

Hadhrat Abul Ahwas narrates, "We once visited Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) as he was with his three sons, who appeared (radiant) like three gold coins. As we looked at the three boys, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) understood our feelings and said, 'It seems like you envy me because of these boys?' We replied, 'It is because of such things that a person is truly the envy of all.' Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) then looked up to the low ceiling of his house where a sparrow had built a nest. He said, 'I prefer dusting off from my hands the sand from the graves of these boys rather than a single egg falling and breaking from that sparrow's nest."

Another narration from Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan states that he used to sit in the company of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) in Kufa. He further says that at that time, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) was married to two beautiful women of high birth and had the most beautiful children from them. As he was sitting on a raised place, a sparrow started chirping from above and then emptied its belly on Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA). As he wiped the mess off, he said, "I prefer that the family of Abdullaah die and I follow them in death rather than this sparrow dying."[^3]
The Statement of Hadhrat Umar (RA) About the Prisoners from Badr

The narration has already passed[^4] concerning the statement that Hadhrat Umar (RA) made about what should be done with the prisoners from the Battle of Badr. He said, "I swear by Allaah that I do not share the opinion of Abu Bakr.
